messages.content: I have the Saturday-through-Friday flight choices now. Compare them for all three of us, including bags. I do not want to pick the hotel area until we know what the flight schedule actually gives us.

Send me the two outbound choices and the three returns, along with the fare type and any bag prices shown. I will compare the six combinations and account for the harbor reservation and time needed to get back to the airport.
Outbound Saturday: Southwest DAL-SAN at 7:10 a.m., arriving 8:20, is $168 each. Frontier DFW-SAN at 1:40 p.m., arriving 2:55, is $109 each. The harbor reservation is at 6:30 that evening.

The Southwest outbound is $504 for three. It includes two checked bags per traveler and allows changes without a change fee, with any eligible balance retained as a flight credit rather than a cash refund on this fare. The Frontier base is $327, but two shared checked bags at $58 each make it $443. Its lowest fare is nonrefundable, and changes or cancellation may carry charges. Southwest gets you to the hotel area before 9:30 a.m.; Frontier leaves little margin between landing, collecting bags, reaching the hotel, checking in, and getting to the harbor.
For Friday, Southwest has 9:05 a.m. SAN-DAL for $139 each and 4:10 p.m. for $169 each. American has SAN-DFW at 1:35 p.m. for $149 each. American charges $40 per checked bag.

For three travelers with two shared checked bags, the 9:05 Southwest return is $417, the American return is $527 including $80 in bag charges, and the 4:10 Southwest return is $507. The Southwest fares retain the same bag and ticket terms as the outbound. The American Main Cabin tickets can generally be changed without a change fee, but a fare difference applies and cancellation produces a trip credit rather than a cash refund.
Lay out the totals. Also tell me when we would realistically have to leave the coast for each return.

With bags included, the six round-trip combinations are: early Southwest outbound plus 9:05 Southwest return, $921; plus 1:35 American, $1,031; plus 4:10 Southwest, $1,011. Late Frontier outbound plus those same returns is $860, $970, or $950. For Friday, allow roughly 35 minutes from the coast plus a two-hour airport cushion: leave about 6:10 a.m. for the 9:05 flight, 10:20 a.m. for American, or 1:00 p.m. for the 4:10 flight. Traffic can increase those transfer times.
So the absolute cheapest pairing costs us most of Saturday and makes us leave before breakfast Friday.

Correct. The $860 pairing saves $151 against the early-outbound, late-return combination, but it gives up nearly six useful hours Saturday and most of Friday morning. It also uses DFW on departure, adds separate bag charges, and puts the 6:30 harbor reservation at risk if the flight or baggage claim runs late.
What about taking the early outbound and the American return? Is there any reason to pay more for that than the late Southwest flight?

Not from these figures. American is $20 more after bags, departs two hours and 35 minutes earlier, and returns to DFW rather than DAL. Its only practical advantage would be if arriving home at 6:15 p.m. instead of 9:05 p.m. matters enough to give up the extra coastal time.
It does not. Select the 7:10 Saturday Southwest outbound and the 4:10 Friday Southwest return. That protects the harbor reservation and lets us keep Friday morning. Do not ticket yet.

Selected as the working itinerary: Saturday Southwest DAL-SAN, 7:10-8:20 a.m., and Friday Southwest SAN-DAL, 4:10-9:05 p.m., for three travelers. The current ticket total is $1,011, including up to two checked bags per traveler. Plan to leave the coast around 1:00 p.m. Friday. This costs $151 more than the cheapest pairing but preserves the first afternoon, protects the 6:30 harbor reservation, and retains Friday morning. Nothing has been ticketed, and the fare, schedule, availability, and exact ticket terms still need live verification. The hotel also remains unbooked; these flight times now support comparing downtown against the coastal locations.
